decision_conditions: <div>Prior to commencement of the development, details of surface water management for the varied works shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the LPA, in consultation with the LLFA. Details shall include: (i) a specification and typical construction build-ups for all new and altered surfacing where permeability is relied upon, (ii) a plan showing the destination and routing of runoff from new and altered hard surfaces, and (iii) a management and maintenance plan for permeable surfaces for the lifetime of the development. The development shall be carried out and thereafter maintained in accordance with the approved details.</div><div><br></div><div>REASON: In the interest of sustainable urban drainage.</div>
<p>No changes to soil levels within the vicinity of the retained trees shall be undertaken.</p><p><br></p><p>REASON: To safeguard the retained trees.</p>

<p>No mechanical excavation shall be undertaken within the root protection areas of retained trees, and any required excavation (for example for the provision of fixings for hard landscaping features such as seating or play equipment) shall be undertaken by hand or using an air space.Any roots exposed shall not be severed.</p><p><br></p><p>REASON: To safeguard the root systems of retained trees.</p>

<p>No hard landscaping features such as benches or play equipment shall be installed within the root protection areas of retained trees until full details of the methods for securing such features have been submitted to, and approved in writing by, the local planning authority. The landscaping features affected shall be installed in full accordance with the details thus approved.</p><p>REASON: To safeguard the root systems of retained trees.</p>

<p>Prior to the commencement of development, </p><p>i) a qualified tree specialist must be appointed to provide arboricultural supervision and inspection;&nbsp;</p><p>ii) The details of this appointment and the specialist's responsibilities must be submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority; and&nbsp;</p><p>iii) The submission should include the methodology and programme for reporting, as well as a timetable for inspections.</p><p>The approved works must be carried out in strict accordance with the approved details. Upon completion of the development, a report from the appointed arboriculturist must be submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority, confirming that all tree protection measures and tree works were carried out in accordance with the approved plans, accompanied by photographs taken at critical stages.<br><br>REASON: to ensure that works affecting trees are carried out in a professional and controlled manner, safeguarding their health and long-term viability. This is in accordance with good arboricultural practice.</p>

Unless otherwise shown on the drawings hereby approved, no tree within the curtilage of the site shall be wilfully damaged or destroyed and no tree shall be removed, lopped, topped, felled or uprooted during the construction of the development hereby approved. Tree protection for all retained trees at the site and on adjacent land shall be undertaken in accordance with BS5837:2012 (Trees in relation to construction - Recommendations) and will protect the root protection area calculated as described in Table 2 of that British Standard for the duration of all site works (including demolition) undertaken in connection with the development hereby approved.No service runs shall be provided within the root protection area of any tree to be retained at the site or on adjacent land. Protective fencing shall be 2.4m high and conform to Figure 2 of BS5837:2012 i.e. a scaffold framework comprising a vertical and horizontal framework, well braced to resist impacts, with vertical tubes spaced at a maximum interval of 3m. On to this weldmesh panels should be securely fixed with wire or scaffold clamps.


REASON: In order to protect the existing trees during building operation and site works.

<p>All hard and soft landscaping works shall be carried out in accordance with the approved details. The works shall be carried out prior to the occupation of any part of the development unless otherwise agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority. Any trees or plants indicated on the approved scheme which, within a period of five years from the date of planting, die, are removed or become seriously damaged, diseased or dying shall be replaced during the next planting season with other trees or plants of a location, species and size to be first approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority.</p><p><br></p><p>REASON: To ensure that the external appearance of the site is acceptable, provides acceptable formal and informal leisure facilities for all ages, and protects and enhances biodiversity, and in accordance with LP47 and LP51 of the Hackney Local Plan as well as Section 15 of the National Planning Policy Framework.</p>

<div>Ecological Mitigation, Enhancement, &amp; Management Plan (EMEMP)</div><div>Prior to the commencement of development, an Ecological Mitigation, Enhancement, &amp; Management Plan (EMEMP) shall be submitted to and approved, in writing, by the local planning authority. The EMEMP must include as a minimum:</div><ul><li>A non-technical summary and details of the roles and responsibilities of the people or organisation(s) delivering the plan;</li><li>Site-specific mitigation measures to minimise adverse effects on biodiversity during construction, including the protection of retained habitats (such as trees) and considerations for nesting birds;</li><li>The planned habitat creation, landscaping scheme, and management measures to maintain all habitats for a minimum period of 10 years from the completion of development (including the replacement of any dead, damaged, or diseased planting); and&nbsp;</li><li>Full specifications, quantities, and precise locations of biodiversity enhancements, including a minimum of 3 bird boxes and 3 bat boxes, embedded into the design of the development in line with local ecological needs.</li></ul><div>The development shall not be undertaken otherwise than in full accordance with the approved details. The approved ecological enhancements (including the bird and bat boxes) shall be fully installed on site prior to the first occupation of the development, and maintained thereafter for the lifetime of the development. Notice shall be given, in writing, to the local planning authority when the EMEMP habitat creation works have been completed.</div><div><br></div><div>REASON:&nbsp; To ensure the development protects, mitigates, and enhances biodiversity and supports urban wildlife populations through effective on-site management and habitat maintenance.</div>
